name: Two-Pointer Technique
explanation: Two pointers iterate over a data structure simultaneously (e.g. left and right boundaries) to evaluate conditions in O(N) time without nested loops.
learning_objectives: Identify sorted array properties suitable for shrinking search spaces
Maintain left and right pointer bounds
Determine clear move criteria for left and right pointers
common_misconceptions: Attempting to use two pointers on unsorted data when sorted order is required
Failing to advance pointers correctly causing infinite loops

no_hint.message: Your pointer manipulation looks solid. Keep monitoring pointer meeting conditions.
no_hint.next_step: Verify your loop condition (e.g. left < right vs left <= right).
no_hint.reflection_question: What condition signals that your search window has collapsed?

concept.message: When an array is sorted, comparing elements at opposite ends allows shrinking the search space in linear time.
concept.next_step: Place one pointer at the beginning and another at the end of your array.
concept.reflection_question: If the current sum is too small, which pointer must move to increase the sum?

guided.message: Compare the sum of elements at left and right pointers against your target.
guided.next_step: If current sum < target, increment left pointer. If sum > target, decrement right pointer.
guided.reflection_question: Why does moving the left pointer right guarantee an increase in sum on a sorted array?

pseudocode.message:
left = 0, right = length - 1
WHILE left < right:
    current_sum = arr[left] + arr[right]
    IF current_sum == target: RETURN [left, right]
    ELSE IF current_sum < target: left++
    ELSE: right--
pseudocode.next_step: Implement the while-loop pointer advancement logic in your code.
pseudocode.reflection_question: How do you handle edge cases where no valid pair exists?

full_solution.message: Using two pointers starting at opposite ends of a sorted array reduces pair finding to O(N) time and O(1) space.
full_solution.next_step: Test with arrays containing negative numbers or duplicate values.
full_solution.reflection_question: What is the advantage of two pointers over hash map lookup in terms of space complexity?

reflection_questions: Why must the input be sorted for the two-pointer directional strategy to hold?
Under what condition should the left pointer advance versus the right pointer?
pseudocode:
left = 0, right = N - 1
WHILE left < right:
    val = arr[left] + arr[right]
    IF val == target: RETURN [left, right]
    IF val < target: left = left + 1
    ELSE: right = right - 1

complexity.time: O(N) - Linear scan shrinking pointer distance
